planNote: Agents choose actions; the simulator calculates every number; you approve.
planMode: Offline planner: deterministic plan search with template explanations (no live language model).
planLive: Claude ({model}) proposed extra plans and wrote the explanations; the simulator computed every number and each figure was checked.
planCached: Replayed from the offline demo cache.
noHot: No station goes over the threshold in this scenario, so the agents recommend no action. Try raising attendance or picking a hot day.
verified: All {n} figures match the simulator output
notVerified: A figure did not match the simulator, so the explanation was withheld.
newHot: Creates a new hotspot at {stations}. The agent flags this trade-off.
replan: Plan applied. Run the agents again to see what else would help.
decisionError: The decision could not be logged, so nothing was applied: {msg}

tourSteps.0: GITEX Global 2025, day 1 at Dubai World Trade Centre. Watch the corridor through the day in the 3D twin.
tourSteps.1: What if it is a hot day? More visitors take the metro, and World Trade Centre station rises above its threshold ring.
tourSteps.2: AI agents propose plans, and the simulator measures each one.
tourSteps.3: You stay in charge: approving the top plan brings every station back under the ring.
tourSteps.4: Try rain, a custom event, or build your own plan in the My plan tab.

glfail: 3D needs WebGL, which is not available in this browser. The table view shows the same results.
canvasAria: 3D digital twin of the Sheikh Zayed Road corridor. Drag to rotate, scroll or pinch to zoom, tap a station to select it. The table view shows the same data.
apiDown: The planning service is not reachable. Showing the last saved results; reconnecting automatically.
publicDemo: Public research demo by SP Jain students. Baseline demand is synthetic and scenario values are assumptions. Not an RTA system and not endorsed by RTA.
how1: Forecast: background demand per station and hour, plus an event surge shared across stations by walking distance.
how2: Capacity: trains per hour from the RTA timetable × train capacity × the share available at one station. Station-hours above the comfort threshold are flagged.
how3: AI agents propose plans from a fixed menu: extra trains, wayfinding, feeder shuttles, robotaxi staging and staggered exits.
how4: A deterministic simulator scores every plan. The agents never calculate numbers; every figure is checked.
how5: Nothing is applied until a human approves it, and every decision is logged.
howAlign: Designed around RTA AI Strategy priorities: congestion reduction, agentic AI and human approval of every decision.
footer: Research prototype by SP Jain MAIB students. Baseline demand is synthetic; attendance, metro share and capacity values are assumptions. Train frequency: RTA open data (GTFS). Map: © OpenStreetMap contributors; building heights are estimated where untagged and sea-side towers are cut to podium height. Not an RTA system and not endorsed by RTA.
